current_leader.name: Merchant settlement acceleration decision engine
current_leader.state_transition: processor balance eligible -> free payout ETA and paid speed tiers known -> external liquidity and obligations reveal actual shortfall -> choose zero/next-day/same-day/instant and minimum amount -> verify acceleration fees avoided
current_leader.why_survived: Fresh families tested this run did not beat it. The leader still has recurring paid-speed events, independent machine-readable balances/ETAs, deterministic marginal fees, and a read-only intervention. The key unresolved issue remains whether paid acceleration materially exceeds genuine liquidity need.
current_leader.strongest_evidence: Prior Adyen/Vagaro evidence establishes repeated instant-payout use; current processor fee ladders make the monetary delta deterministic.
current_leader.closest_threat: First-party payout controls plus treasury forecasting can absorb the wedge; exact cross-system minimum-necessary-acceleration functionality remains unconfirmed.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read PSP balances, settlement ETAs and fee tiers plus bank liquidity and near-term obligations; recommend no acceleration or the cheapest sufficient speed and minimum amount. No custody or payout execution.
current_leader.monetization: Small per-success recommendation fee, micro subscription, or capped share of verified acceleration fees avoided versus competent cash management.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Repeated accelerated payouts may be rational working-capital demand rather than avoidable leakage.
current_leader.next_research_test: Find merchant-level or anonymized evidence connecting accelerated payout amounts to external liquidity and obligations; calculate avoidable acceleration ratio. Kill if immaterial or if an exact incumbent is found.

candidates_tested.fatal_flaw: Gate 8: exact or sufficiently close AP products already track and automatically apply vendor credits before payment, while recovery-audit software explicitly detects missed credits and overpayments.

candidates_tested.why: The daily 10% cloud-services billing threshold is real and machine-readable, but Snowflake already documents direct remediation for dynamic tables and several Snowflake FinOps products continuously optimize cloud-services/compute. A timing-only wedge is narrow and risks becoming ordinary Snowflake cost optimization.

candidates_tested.fatal_flaw: Gate 8 / monetization: Twilio itself identifies inactive numbers using traffic/configuration status, explicitly recommends releasing them to stop recurring charges, and exposes API deletion. The residual wedge is too close to a first-party checklist/checkbox.
Gate 8: multiple exact hotel products audit OTA commissions for cancellations, no-shows, wrong rates, and virtual-card gaps and prepare/execute recovery workflows.

new_search_rules: If the first party already exposes both an inactivity signal and the exact one-click/API cost-elimination action, treat the wedge as a likely checkbox rather than a defensible programmable tollbooth unless a materially richer cross-system decision remains.

Threshold quirks such as Snowflake's daily included-credit boundary are not enough by themselves; prove that timing/reconfiguration creates incremental savings beyond first-party documented remediation and existing FinOps optimizers.
